The leg hooks avoid this by using `== 'legname'`; the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

**⚠️ IMPORTANT — `daily_publish_report.sh:172`**: `leg_ceiling_minutes` interpolates the job-name fragment into an awk ERE unescaped. The CLI fragment (`Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`, no parenthetical for `${prefix%% (*}` to strip) contains `+`, so the regex can never match the workflow yaml — verified live: CLI returns empty while testflight/play/pubdev return correct ceilings. A cancelled CLI leg silently loses its timeout-ceiling section (an AC2 gap).

## PR Description

Closes #1478
### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart
```
Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10089 passed, 10 skipped.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[Failed/cancelled leg] --> FS[failing steps via jobs API]
  LEG --> LE[log_excerpt]
  LE -->|child run| CF[gh run view --log-failed]
  LE -->|own run / mid-run| PJ[gh run view --job id --log]
  CF --> SE[signal_excerpt: first 3 signal matches +/-3 ctx]
  PJ --> SE
  SE -->|no signal| TAIL[raw tail fallback]
  SE --> SIG[error_signature: priority-class line, normalized]
  SIG --> SEARCH[gh search issues --match body,comments]
  SEARCH -->|match| CMT[comment on root-cause issue]
  SEARCH -->|no match| TITLE[leg-title dedup -> comment or file]
```

</details>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily auto-publish report (issue #161): renders the per-run job-summary
# table and drives the self-healing issue lifecycle.
#
#   failing/cancelled leg -> file a bug issue assigned to the owner; dedup
#     guard: an OPEN issue labeled `daily-publish` with the same title gets
#     a fresh comment (new run link + log excerpt) instead of a duplicate
#   green leg -> auto-close that leg's still-open issue with a comment
#
# Inputs come from environment (set by the daily-publish.yml report job):
#   PLAN_RESULT         needs.plan.result — a plan failure files its own issue
#   LEG_<NAME>          needs result: success | failure | skipped | cancelled
#   LEG_<NAME>_URL      child run URL (empty on internal/skip paths)
#   LEG_PUBDEV_*        status (up-to-date/private/recovered/release-in-flight),
#                       versions, tag-run URL
#   NEXT_TAG            estimated next tag (informational; legs derive latest+1 themselves)
#   GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL   runner defaults
#
# Exits non-zero when any leg failed or was cancelled (the daily run goes
# red too); all-skipped stays green (#159 lesson).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
next_tag="${NEXT_TAG:-}"
failed_legs=""
actions=""
rows="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$rows"' EXIT

gh label create daily-publish --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── log collection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Failing job/step names and the last ~50 log lines, from the child run when
# one exists, else from this daily run's leg job (jobs API — the run is
# still in progress here, and GitHub serves no logs for it mid-run).
failing_steps() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --json jobs --jq '
      [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
        | .name + " — " +
          ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
            | .name] | join(", "))]
      | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    # The report job runs INSIDE the daily run, so the run is still in
    # progress here — and GitHub serves no logs for in-progress runs
    # (--log-failed returns empty: issue #208 was filed as "unknown (job
    # cancelled or timed out)" for a leg that died in 4s with a clear
    # error). Job/step data IS served mid-run — read failed steps from it.
    gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
      | jq -r --arg job "$2" '
          [.jobs[] | select(.name == $job
                              and (.conclusion == "failure"
                                or .conclusion == "cancelled"))
            | .name + " — " +
              ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure"
                               or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                | .name] | join(", "))]
          | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────

    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too

          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}

blocks.text:
Important observation: The "Verify injected-failure excerpt" step in the workflow searches for the open issue by title `[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed`. But with the root-cause dedup, the report may instead comment on a root-cause issue and NOT create an issue with that title. In the inject_failure case, if the injected `::error::` line happens to match an open issue's body/comments via the signature search, then no issue with title `[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed` would be created, and the verify step would fail the run with "no open issue titled ... — the self-filing path regressed". That's a potential false positive in the TEST hook, but inject_failure is a controlled test hook, so the injected line is unique and unlikely to match. Low risk, edge case.

Also worth noting: the verify step checks issue body AND comments: `--json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)'`. That looks fine.

Another thing to check: In the workflow verify step, if title-dedup fires (existing issue gets a comment), the issue titled the same exists — fine.

Now, deeper review of the shell script:

1. **`frag="${prefix%% (*}"`** — prefix is "Leg: $2", e.g. "Leg: Play (Android beta)". frag becomes "Leg: Play". The yaml job name for play is "Leg: Play (Android external beta)" — note the workflow display name in the test fixture yaml is "Leg: Play (Android external beta)" but the report display name is "Play (Android beta)". So the fragment "Leg: Play" matches via `contains`. Good.

But wait — check the yaml: what's the actual play leg job name in daily-publish.yml? The PR description says "the yaml display names add parentheticals the report's display names don't carry". Let me check the actual job names. Also the check for testflight: yaml name "Leg: TestFlight" and report prefix "Leg: TestFlight" — frag = "Leg: TestFlight" (no parenthetical). contains works.

Potential collision: "Leg: Play" is a fragment of only play. "Leg: CLI" only cli. OK.

2. **`log_excerpt` for child run path**: `tail -n 400` of `--log-failed` output, then signal_excerpt. If raw is empty (child in flight or cancelled), falls to per-job path with `$GITHUB_RUN_ID` (this daily run). Note: for a child run that concluded cancelled/failure, `--log-failed` should return the log; but if the child was cancelled before any step failed, `--log-failed` returns empty, and then per-job resolution resolves the LEG job (watcher) in the current run — good for the cancelled digest.

Edge: `gh run view "$1" --log-failed` failing returns empty, fallback per-job gets own-run job log. OK.

3. **`signal_excerpt` awk**: stores all lines in memory (`lines[NR]=$0`), tail capped at 400 lines so bounded. Fine.

Signal regex includes `FAIL` with `(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL` — matches "FAIL" at start or preceded by non-letter. OK.

One subtlety: `want[i]=1` for hits<=3, but hits continues incrementing beyond 3 — fine since only first 3 matches mark context.

4. **`error_signature`**: takes first line of the highest-priority class. Then `awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}'` strips the job/step prefix columns (gh log format is `job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp<TAB>message`? Actually `gh run view --log` format is `jobname\tstepname\ttimestamp\tmessage`? Let me recall: gh run view --log output is `job\tstep\ttimestamp\tlog line`? The gh log format: `jobname\tstepname\ttimestamp\tlog message`. Hmm, actually the real format from GitHub's log endpoint is `job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp<TAB>message`. `awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}'` takes the last field = the message. But wait — if the log message itself contains tabs, $NF is only text after the last tab. Logs with tabs are rare. OK.

But there's a subtlety: the sed strips `^::error::` only at line start. The signature from the injected log: `::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — ...` → after tab-strip: `2026-10-10T05:17:12.0000Z ::error::injected failure ...`. Then sed strips the timestamp: `s/^[0-9]\{4\}-...Z *//` — the timestamp format is `2026-10-10T05:17:12.0000Z` — pattern `[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z` matches `05:17:12.0000Z`. Yes. Then strips `^::error::`. Good.

Then in `find_issue_by_signature`: `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' '` converts everything not in that set to spaces — collapses runs. Note: this keeps `-` and `+` and `. Then wraps in quotes for search: `"$q"`. The query could contain characters like `(` — no, those get converted to space. Search query with quoted phrase — GitHub search requires the phrase; fine.

blocks.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo + extension
#                                 + the /outlook add-in slice)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: verify step runs (and fails) on every scheduled daily run**

`inject_failure` is a `workflow_dispatch`-only input (`default: none`). On `schedule` triggers — the primary daily use of this workflow — the GitHub Actions `inputs` context is **empty**, so `inputs.inject_failure` evaluates to `''`, not `'none'`. Therefore:

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

is **true on every cron run**. The step then computes `title="[daily-publish]  leg failed"` (empty `INJECTED`), finds no such open issue, and hits `exit 1` — turning the report job (and thus the whole daily run) red **every single day**, even when all legs are green. The dispatch default only applies to `workflow_dispatch` events; it does not populate `inputs` for `schedule`.

The existing leg hooks use `== 'testflight'` etc., which is safe precisely because empty never equals a leg name — the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

Fix (either):

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

or guard in-script (more robust against any future trigger that lacks inputs):

```bash
[ -n "${INJECTED}" ] || { echo "no inject_failure input — nothing to verify"; exit 0; }
```
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `leg_ceiling_minutes` silently misses the CLI leg — the awk regex breaks on `+` in the fragment**

`file_or_comment` derives the fragment with `frag="${prefix%% (*}"`, which only strips a ` (` parenthetical. For the CLI leg the report display is `CLI + macOS desktop` (no parenthetical), so `frag` is the literal `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`. That string is then interpolated **unescaped** into an awk ERE:

```awk
$0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
```

`+` is a regex operator, so the pattern `name: .Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` can never match the workflow line `name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'` — after the space-run matched by ` +`, the pattern demands `macOS` but the text has `+ macOS`. Verified against the real `daily-publish.yml`:

- `Leg: TestFlight` → `360` ✅
- `Leg: Play` → `240` ✅
- `Leg: pub.dev` → `60` ✅
- `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` → **empty** ❌

Result: a cancelled CLI leg gets "Cancelled while running: job … killed after X elapsed." with **no timeout ceiling and no elapsed-vs-ceiling verdict** — an AC2 gap for one of the six legs (and the new test's fixture yaml uses `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` as a job name but never asserts its ceiling, so the gap is invisible in CI).

Fix — match the fragment literally instead of as a regex, e.g.:

```awk
index($0, "name: ") == 1 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
```

or escape `frag` with `gsub(/[][\\.^$*+?()|]/, "\\\\&", frag)` before building the pattern.

## Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES (1 blocking, 1 important, 2 suggestions)

The gh-1478 rework is fundamentally strong — signal-first excerpts, the per-job log fallback (correctly diagnosing the 409 mid-run zip), cancelled-run digests, and signature-based root-cause dedup all satisfy the ticket ACs, with 13 new behavioral tests passing plus the 51 release-flow tests. But two defects need fixing:

**🚨 BLOCKING — `daily-publish.yml:596`**: `if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'` is **true on every `schedule` run**. `inject_failure` is a `workflow_dispatch`-only input; on cron triggers the `inputs` context is empty (`''`), so the new verify step runs daily, looks for an issue titled `[daily-publish]  leg failed` (empty `INJECTED`), finds none, and `exit 1` — turning the report job red every single day. The leg hooks avoid this by using `== 'legname'`; the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

**⚠️ IMPORTANT — `daily_publish_report.sh:172`**: `leg_ceiling_minutes` interpolates the job-name fragment into an awk ERE unescaped. The CLI fragment (`Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`, no parenthetical for `${prefix%% (*}` to strip) contains `+`, so the regex can never match the workflow yaml — verified live: CLI returns empty while testflight/play/pubdev return correct ceilings. A cancelled CLI leg silently loses its timeout-ceiling section (an AC2 gap).

**💡 Suggestions**: add a cancelled-CLI ceiling test (the gap that let the regex bug through), and fix the `fmt_elapsed` comment (`1h02m03s` promised, `1h2m3s` produced).

Also noted in the general comment (unchanged code, no thread): `failing_steps`' own-run path exact-matches the play leg's display prefix against a yaml job name that differs, yielding "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" — worth passing `frag` there in a follow-up.

## PR Description

Closes #1478
### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart
```
Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10089 passed, 10 skipped.

  CF --> SE[signal_excerpt: first 3 signal matches +/-3 ctx]

  SIG --> SEARCH[gh search issues --match body,comments]
  SEARCH -->|match| CMT[comment on root-cause issue]

```

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

```awk

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily auto-publish report (issue #161): renders the per-run job-summary
# table and drives the self-healing issue lifecycle.
#
#   failing/cancelled leg -> file a bug issue assigned to the owner; dedup
#     guard: an OPEN issue labeled `daily-publish` with the same title gets
#     a fresh comment (new run link + log excerpt) instead of a duplicate
#   green leg -> auto-close that leg's still-open issue with a comment
#
# Inputs come from environment (set by the daily-publish.yml report job):
#   PLAN_RESULT         needs.plan.result — a plan failure files its own issue
#   LEG_<NAME>          needs result: success | failure | skipped | cancelled
#   LEG_<NAME>_URL      child run URL (empty on internal/skip paths)
#   LEG_PUBDEV_*        status (up-to-date/private/recovered/release-in-flight),
#                       versions, tag-run URL
#   NEXT_TAG            estimated next tag (informational; legs derive latest+1 themselves)
#   GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL   runner defaults
#
# Exits non-zero when any leg failed or was cancelled (the daily run goes
# red too); all-skipped stays green (#159 lesson).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
next_tag="${NEXT_TAG:-}"
failed_legs=""
actions=""
rows="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$rows"' EXIT

gh label create daily-publish --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── log collection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Failing job/step names and the last ~50 log lines, from the child run when
# one exists, else from this daily run's leg job (jobs API — the run is
# still in progress here, and GitHub serves no logs for it mid-run).
failing_steps() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --json jobs --jq '
      [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
        | .name + " — " +
          ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
            | .name] | join(", "))]
      | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    # The report job runs INSIDE the daily run, so the run is still in
    # progress here — and GitHub serves no logs for in-progress runs
    # (--log-failed returns empty: issue #208 was filed as "unknown (job
    # cancelled or timed out)" for a leg that died in 4s with a clear
    # error). Job/step data IS served mid-run — read failed steps from it.
    gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
      | jq -r --arg job "$2" '
          [.jobs[] | select(.name == $job
                              and (.conclusion == "failure"
                                or .conclusion == "cancelled"))
            | .name + " — " +
              ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure"
                               or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                | .name] | join(", "))]
          | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

Important observation: The "Verify injected-failure excerpt" step in the workflow searches for the open issue by title `[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed`. But with the root-cause dedup, the report may instead comment on a root-cause issue and NOT create an issue with that title. In the inject_failure case, if the injected `::error::` line happens to match an open issue's body/comments via the signature search, then no issue with title `[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed` would be created, and the verify step would fail the run with "no open issue titled ... — the self-filing path regressed". That's a potential false positive in the TEST hook, but inject_failure is a controlled test hook, so the injected line is unique and unlikely to match. Low risk, edge case.

Also worth noting: the verify step checks issue body AND comments: `--json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)'`. That looks fine.

blocks.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo + extension
#                                 + the /outlook add-in slice)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: verify step runs (and fails) on every scheduled daily run**

`inject_failure` is a `workflow_dispatch`-only input (`default: none`). On `schedule` triggers — the primary daily use of this workflow — the GitHub Actions `inputs` context is **empty**, so `inputs.inject_failure` evaluates to `''`, not `'none'`. Therefore:

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

is **true on every cron run**. The step then computes `title="[daily-publish]  leg failed"` (empty `INJECTED`), finds no such open issue, and hits `exit 1` — turning the report job (and thus the whole daily run) red **every single day**, even when all legs are green. The dispatch default only applies to `workflow_dispatch` events; it does not populate `inputs` for `schedule`.

The existing leg hooks use `== 'testflight'` etc., which is safe precisely because empty never equals a leg name — the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

Fix (either):

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

or guard in-script (more robust against any future trigger that lacks inputs):

```bash
[ -n "${INJECTED}" ] || { echo "no inject_failure input — nothing to verify"; exit 0; }
```
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `leg_ceiling_minutes` silently misses the CLI leg — the awk regex breaks on `+` in the fragment**

`file_or_comment` derives the fragment with `frag="${prefix%% (*}"`, which only strips a ` (` parenthetical. For the CLI leg the report display is `CLI + macOS desktop` (no parenthetical), so `frag` is the literal `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`. That string is then interpolated **unescaped** into an awk ERE:

```awk
$0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
```

`+` is a regex operator, so the pattern `name: .Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` can never match the workflow line `name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'` — after the space-run matched by ` +`, the pattern demands `macOS` but the text has `+ macOS`. Verified against the real `daily-publish.yml`:

- `Leg: TestFlight` → `360` ✅
- `Leg: Play` → `240` ✅
- `Leg: pub.dev` → `60` ✅
- `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` → **empty** ❌

Result: a cancelled CLI leg gets "Cancelled while running: job … killed after X elapsed." with **no timeout ceiling and no elapsed-vs-ceiling verdict** — an AC2 gap for one of the six legs (and the new test's fixture yaml uses `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` as a job name but never asserts its ceiling, so the gap is invisible in CI).

Fix — match the fragment literally instead of as a regex, e.g.:

```awk
index($0, "name: ") == 1 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
```

or escape `frag` with `gsub(/[][\\.^$*+?()|]/, "\\\\&", frag)` before building the pattern.

## Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES (1 blocking, 1 important, 2 suggestions)

The gh-1478 rework is fundamentally strong — signal-first excerpts, the per-job log fallback (correctly diagnosing the 409 mid-run zip), cancelled-run digests, and signature-based root-cause dedup all satisfy the ticket ACs, with 13 new behavioral tests passing plus the 51 release-flow tests. The leg hooks avoid this by using `== 'legname'`; the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

**⚠️ IMPORTANT — `daily_publish_report.sh:172`**: `leg_ceiling_minutes` interpolates the job-name fragment into an awk ERE unescaped. The CLI fragment (`Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`, no parenthetical for `${prefix%% (*}` to strip) contains `+`, so the regex can never match the workflow yaml — verified live: CLI returns empty while testflight/play/pubdev return correct ceilings. A cancelled CLI leg silently loses its timeout-ceiling section (an AC2 gap).

**💡 Suggestions**: add a cancelled-CLI ceiling test (the gap that let the regex bug through), and fix the `fmt_elapsed` comment (`1h02m03s` promised, `1h2m3s` produced).

## PR Description

Closes #1478
### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.
